Crocodile: Long narrower crocodile snout with visible lower tooth, scuted trunk and complete curved tail. Four feet readable but far proximal limbs partly hidden by the belly; foot levels differ. Tail and snout approach the 8% border. No external ear pinnae are present.
Monitor Lizard: Dark spotted monitor with complete banded tail, long neck, forked tongue and four clawed feet. Head is raised naturally above feet, but forelimbs are relatively pillar-like, far roots remain obscured and near/far feet differ in height. Tail and tongue approach the border; no framing admission inferred.
Anole: Green slender anole with orange-red dewlap, long complete tail, four bent legs and expanded toe tips. Dewlap partly occludes the far shoulder; far hip also overlaps the trunk. Feet differ in height and tail tip is near the left border. Dewlap ownership requires a real source-specific boundary.
Skink: Smooth glossy overlapping scales, long cylindrical trunk, striped sides, short natural limbs and full long tail. Four feet are visible but far hind shaft is almost entirely hidden under the belly; cannot claim four exposed limb chains. Feet sit at different vertical levels. Tail approaches left margin.
Mountain Lizard: Mottled brown rocky-colour lizard with complete tapering tail and four clawed feet. Far hind upper leg is hidden under the belly, and contacts differ in height. Natural bent near limbs are readable; no external ear pinnae. Source needs truthful far-chain authoring assessment.
Lizard: Brown and green mottled lacertid-like lizard with visible scales, full banded tail and four feet. Near fore/hind joint bends readable; far hind leg is largely occluded by the trunk with only its lower section exposed. Unequal contact levels remain. No ear pinnae.
Whiptail: Slender striped body with very long complete whip tail, pointed snout and four separate feet. Near/far distal shafts are distinct, though far attachments remain behind the trunk. Contacts at differing heights; tail tip near left margin. Natural tail length retained rather than shortened.
Agama: Orange-red head and throat, blue body and banded full tail; four distinct distal legs with natural bends. The pronounced spiny neck/dorsal fringe and hanging throat flap need species-identity review rather than automatic anatomy acceptance. Far roots remain partly behind the trunk and feet differ in height.
Gila Monster: Black and orange beaded scales, broad blunt head and thick short tail are clear. Four clawed feet are visible; near fore/hind chains are distinct, far proximal roots partially occluded and feet at different levels. Tail is unusually swollen/blunt and needs canonical identity judgment. No external ear pinnae.
Frilled Lizard: Large orange/brown spread neck frill, open mouth, long complete curved tail and four visible feet. Frill is displayed rather than relaxed and hides shoulder roots; far hind root also obscured. Unequal foot heights persist. This is a display-pose source hold, not the requested quiet planted stance.
Chameleon: Tall casque, turret eye, compressed green/orange patterned body and coiled tail identify a veiled-type chameleon. Four feet are visible but their spread clawed digits do not clearly form the required opposed grasping groups; anatomical foot hold. Far limb roots partly behind body, uneven contacts and closely nested tail coils need authoring review.
Marine Iguana: Dark scaly body with red mottling, blunt salt-encrusted snout and dorsal spines; four clawed feet readable. Tail terminates in a fan-like paddle with ray-like ridges rather than an unambiguously natural tapered iguana tail: anatomical source hold. Far proximal limbs obscured and contacts uneven.
Giraffe: Long neck, reticulated brown patches, two ossicones and two visible ears; four long hoofed legs and complete tufted tail. Head/front body angled slightly toward viewer, making both ears readable. Far foreleg root partly behind chest and near foreleg; contact levels nearly align but require exact scoring. Not a strict planar side profile.
Buffalo: Massive dark buffalo, joined horn boss, both natural drooping ears, four hooves and complete tufted tail. Near/far lower legs separated with nearly level contacts; upper far foreleg still merges into chest silhouette. Head faces partly toward viewer, allowing ears but differing from strict side request. Coarse coat and muddy surface do not imply acceptance.
Banteng: Brown bovine with white stockings and rump patch, upward-curved horns, both ears and full tufted tail. Four hoof endpoints and separated lower legs readable; far proximal foreleg remains partly behind trunk. Slight three-quarter head with one visible eye. Retain exact source, no semantic presence inferred.
Water Buffalo: Broad long swept horns, both actual ears, sparse dark coat and four hoof endpoints; complete tufted tail. Far upper foreleg remains behind near chest/leg; hind roots also share trunk silhouette. Near/far contacts close but not identical. Slight head turn preserves both ears without inventing detached parts.
Tamarin: Small rusty-brown primate with long complete non-gripping tail, white crest/moustache and four clawed hand/foot endpoints. Paint combines a cotton-top-like crest with emperor-like moustache; generic canonical representative still needs species-identity judgment. Far upper limbs partly hidden by fur/trunk and contacts at different heights; no branch painted.
Langur: Pale grey slender long-limbed monkey with black face/hands, crown crest and a complete tail longer than trunk. Two hands and two feet are visible; far forelimb is stretched forward, and all contacts are not level. Far ear/upper roots partly hidden by fur/head; no hidden anatomy claim.
Monkey: Brown capuchin-like monkey with pale face, dark crown, grasping hands/feet and a complete curling tail. Four endpoints visible but rightmost hand is lifted/curled, so four planted contacts are not established. Far ear hidden and upper chains partly occluded. Retain source as a first generic-monkey painting, not a fit.
Mandrill: Red nose stripe, ridged blue cheeks, olive-gold mane, high shoulders and short upright stump tail are readable. Two hands and two feet are visible with close but unequal contact levels. Heavy mane obscures far shoulder; one ear hidden. Face turns toward viewer rather than strict side; preserve actual visible ownership only.
Marmoset: Small mottled brown/grey primate with white fan ear tufts and a long visibly banded tail. Four clawed hand/foot endpoints present, but far limb roots remain hidden by torso fur and feet do not share a single level. Ear tufts obscure ear anatomy; do not treat tufts as proven separate ears.
Aye-Aye: Huge naked ears, golden eyes, coarse dark coat and very large shaggy tail. The forward hand is lifted and several digits appear greatly elongated rather than one unmistakable specialized middle finger; anatomy/contact hold. Four extremities visible but only three can read as supports. Far root partly obscured; tail strands need honest contour ownership.
Proboscis Monkey: Pendulous male nose, orange-brown back, pale grey limbs/tail and rounded belly present. Four hand/foot endpoints visible, but forearms cross/overlap and the far hand is behind the near wrist rather than separately exposed from its shoulder. Unequal contact heights and hidden far ear remain holds.
